title: Warehouse vs Lake vs Lakehouse (Platform View)

scenes.heading: Warehouse vs Lake vs Lakehouse
scenes.narration: Three platform patterns dominate analytics today, and knowing their trade-offs helps you pick the right foundation.

scenes.heading: The three patterns
bullets: Data warehouse: structured, governed, SQL-first, and query-optimized.
Data lake: cheap object storage holding raw files in any format.
Lakehouse: open table formats add warehouse features on top of a lake.
The line between them is blurring as warehouses read lakes directly.
scenes.narration: A warehouse gives you governed, structured, high-performance SQL. A lake gives you cheap, flexible storage for raw data of any shape. A lakehouse tries to blend the two by layering table formats like Delta and Iceberg over lake storage.

scenes.heading: Warehouse vs data lake

right.title: Data lake
points: Needs an engine to query well

scenes.narration: Warehouses enforce structure on write, which brings governance and fast queries at a higher storage cost. Lakes store anything cheaply but defer structure until read time, so you need a query engine to make sense of them. Use a warehouse for trusted BI and a lake for cheap, raw, exploratory data.

scenes.heading: How the lakehouse bridges them
steps: Store raw files in the lake
scenes.narration: The lakehouse keeps data in cheap open storage but wraps it in table formats that add ACID transactions and schema management. That lets a query engine treat lake files like warehouse tables. You get much of the warehouse experience without duplicating data into a separate system.

scenes.text: Warehouses optimize for governed SQL, lakes for cheap raw storage, and lakehouses aim to give you both.
scenes.narration: Pick a warehouse for governed performance, a lake for cheap flexibility, or a lakehouse when you want to move toward both at once.
